title: Choose the visual world for the ReelFlies home page
question: The roll assigned Streamside Stone. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Streamside Stone
options.lineage: Flies laid out on wet slate at the river's edge, the way the ReelFlies banners are already shot
options.thesis: The home page is the rock an angler empties a box onto: real flies laid out on slate, picked up and added right there.
materials: white specimen cards, photos as shot
options.viewport: A slate field across the fold: the H1, search and the two ways in (what it is, what it catches) on the left; best sellers laid on the stone as white specimen cards with price per fly and a working + Add on the right; the order line pinned below.
options.risk: Grey stone can read cold or precious; it leans on real slate photography (six banners today), and needs a dense, plain-spoken shop rhythm to stay clear of boutique.

raised.raise: Light marks state: at rest the stone sits in shade; the fly you point at catches raking light, and every fly you've added keeps a lit edge.
Hot-spot orange is held for one job, buying: + Add, Add to cart and the cart count, nowhere else on the page.
Every name governs flies: point at a Fly Type or a Species and the flies it covers surface on the stone while the rest recede.
One pinned order line carries the live state: flies, patterns, total, and what's left to free shipping.
What you add is visibly placed: each added fly drops into your box on the order line, so the order is something you can see.
Sizes step like a test strip: one stepped band, largest hook to smallest, previews a pattern's sizes before you commit.

options.label: The Open Fly Box
options.lineage: The angler's own fly box: slotted foam rows under a clear lid
options.thesis: The page is your fly box: each foam row a Fly Type or a Species, and every fly you add is seated in a slot of your own box.
options.viewport: An open box fills the fold: the lid carries the logo, H1 and search; the foam rows below hold best sellers in slots, each with price per fly and + Add.
options.risk: The most familiar idea in the category: fly-box imagery is every fly shop's first move, and compartment rows drift toward a plain product grid.

options.label: Plankton Wake
options.thesis: Flies surface in a black sea only where the pointer's glowing wake passes.
options.viewport: A black field where flies glow into view along the pointer's wake.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a night ocean says nothing to river anglers, and flies hidden in darkness fail the shop.
options.kept: Light marks state: what's active lights up, everything at rest recedes.
options.risk: Products invisible at rest; heavy GPU work on phones.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.thesis: Each fly shown like a fired vessel: soot black, crackle silver, one ember-hot thing.
options.viewport: A soot-black field with one ember-lit fly as the hero and stage labels stacked like kiln logs.
options.case: Fuses poorly: kiln ritual means nothing to anglers, and its stages don't map to buying flies.
options.kept: Total palette discipline: the hot colour belongs to one thing only.
options.risk: Reads as a craft gallery, not a shop.

options.label: Character Reference Sheet
options.thesis: A fly drawn in four views with its tying materials as named swatches.
options.viewport: One fly in four views, a swatch row of its materials, hand-lettered notes in the gaps.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the amateur clash cheapens the tying, and one fly in depth hides the range.
options.kept: Every name governs what it covers: a label highlights the parts it controls.
options.risk: Reads amateur and tips toward discount.

options.label: Signal Degradation
options.thesis: The shop as a channel: colour bars, burned-in timecode and a repeating crawl.
options.viewport: Colour bars and a stand-by card, with the offer running in the crawl.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no angler identifies with it, and the noise fights the photography.
options.kept: One pinned line carries the live state.

options.label: Minihompy Room
options.thesis: A fly room you furnish with the flies you add, with a visitor ledger.
options.viewport: An isometric pastel room where each added fly appears as a furnishing.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a Korean social-web room is foreign to Canadian anglers and buries the catalogue.
options.kept: What you add is visibly placed and stays where you put it.
options.risk: Cute, slow, and far from the shop's voice.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Choosing flies as a darkroom sequence under amber safelight, with test strips.
options.viewport: Amber-washed stations in order (choose, size, add), with test strips previewing sizes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: anglers don't live in darkrooms, and the amber wash falsifies the flies' colours.
options.kept: Stepped strips preview before you commit.
options.risk: Colour-cast product photos; a slow staged flow.

canonCard.label: The fly-shop standard
canonCard.thesis: What fly shops ship: a river hero with a Shop button, category tiles, best sellers, a story block and a newsletter.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed river photo with the headline and a Shop flies button; six category tiles below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the big fly shops by design, and no lifestyle river photography is on file today.
